A second tied each capsule of a capsule network to one attribute and built the malignancy output from attribute prototypes; in a study with six radiologists, the attribute scores and prototypes tended to raise diagnostic accuracy when the model was right and to lower it when the model was wrong [38].

The prototypical part network classifies an image by comparing its parts with learned prototypes [62]; it has been applied to breast tomosynthesis with assessment through radiologist feedback [63], but no peer-reviewed prototype network for chest CT was found other than the attribute prototypes described above [38].

Attribute explanations tended to lower accuracy when the model was wrong [38], region prompts were associated with missed cancers when the tool missed them [83], and heat maps reduced but did not remove automation bias [82].
